svg.title: Completeness on real TOIs by planet radius, with published references
svg.desc: Blind benchmark on 662 real TESS Objects of Interest (NASA Exoplanet Archive TOI table, fetched 2026-10-19, seed 20261019), held-out half, the three Probes. Completeness, the share of confirmed or known planets (CP/KP) on searchable stars recovered as a vetted dip on the ephemeris, with Wilson 95% intervals: overall 57% (86/150, 49%–65%). By planet radius: < 2 R⊕: 10% (2/20, 3%–30%); 2–4 R⊕: 23% (6/26, 11%–42%); 4–8 R⊕: 36% (4/11, 15%–65%); > 8 R⊕: 80% (73/91, 71%–87%). By period: 0.5–2 d: 41% (12/29, 26%–59%); 2–5 d: 67% (52/78, 56%–76%); 5–13 d: 51% (22/43, 37%–65%). Excluding the stars exposed to the known clipping bug: 53% (65/123). Published references, as stated in the report: Kepler Robovetter DR25 above 85% for P < 100 d (Thompson et al. 2018); Planet Hunters TESS 85% above 4 R⊕ and 51% at 3–4 R⊕ (Eisner et al. 2021). SetuHQ is below both. Measured on a stated benchmark, not discoveries. Sources: docs/results/benchmark_real_tois.json and docs/results/benchmark_real_tois.md, commit 1180dfe.
